name: Maseru
subtitle: Maseru, capital of Lesotho: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 343,541 people live in the Maseru urban centre (counted 2016).
Maseru was proclaimed the capital of the Basotho people in 1869 by Moshoeshoe I, when it was a modest trading outpost.

In the same year colonial forces made Maseru administrative headquarters of the British Basutoland Protectorate. (Note: other sources say it began as a British police camp; accounts differ on who founded it.)

parts.text: Maseru was proclaimed the capital of the Basotho people in 1869 by Moshoeshoe I, when it was a modest trading outpost.

In the same year colonial forces made Maseru administrative headquarters of the British Basutoland Protectorate. (Note: other sources say it began as a British police camp; accounts differ on who founded it.)
Since then the city has expanded rapidly, with problems such as poverty and overcrowding.

parts.text: 343,541 in 2016, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Maseru urban centre, 2016 census (Lesotho Bureau of Statistics figures as compiled by citypopulation.de).

items.text: Maseru proclaimed capital of the Basotho and made administrative headquarters of the British Basutoland Protectorate.
Constitutional governance restored after several years of military rule.
Disputed elections led to violent unrest that left much of Maseru in ruins.
During the South African-led intervention, most of Maseru's central business district was burned and looted.
Lesotho's sixth scientific census was conducted; Maseru district held about a quarter of the population.
